0.text: I wish I were anywhere else. I wish I were SOMEONE else.

1.text: That was my second time setting out and I didn't find a single ray of sunlight. (Or moonlight, for that matter.)

2.text: I must have tumbled through some sort of tunnel to get here, but it's not showing up anywhere.

3.text: Even a glint of sunshine would give me an idea of how long I've been down here for.

4.text: My phone still won't turn on, and the ceiling's just a craggy mess that I can't make out most of the time.

5.text: On top of that, the food in my backpack really hasn't stretched far.

6.text: If I ever see Joe again, I'm going to tell him what an awful idea this trip was.

7.text: I know that solar eclipses are rare, particularly total ones, but it wasn't worth this crisis.

8.text: When Nick and I agreed to this, I really liked the idea of traveling out west and camping with our friends for a few nights.

9.text: Now I don't know if I'll see any of them again.

10.text: I think I'll need to try drinking the water around here soon, although that faint glow (among other things) concerns me.

11.text: I can add that to the list of things I've been having trouble explaining lately.

12.text: Even if I can't drink from them, the pools ARE illuminating the cavern a surprising amount.

13.text: Though, I'm afraid to wander too close to the long, jagged shadows they're casting.

0.text: Those other shadows were contorted. Writhing. Like thousands of hands reaching out towards us.

1.text: They felt so cold as they closed in on our feet.

2.text: In retrospect, I really don't know where we were trying to run to.

3.text: We were surrounded by trees, and the trail would have only taken us deeper into the woods.

5.text: I'm completely useless on my own.

6.text: I don't think I'm ever going to find my way out.

7.text: Even if anyone else ended up down here, all I've heard are dull echoes in the distance.

0.text: Even after all of that, I think I should get back up and head out again.

1.text: Why sit here and "rest up" to delay the inevitable?

2.text: Yes, it's time to get going, Mary.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Wait, is that a person? People?

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Ah, no, wha . . . what are you?!?

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Ungh, feeling dizzy, it's getting closer.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Probably wasn't going to make it out of here anyways.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Umm . . . maybe . . . if it's going to get me no matter what . . .

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: I can't believe I'm about to do this.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: But, how did you get here? Where did you come from?

2.speaker: Mary
2.text: What?!? What do you mean you don't know?

3.speaker: Joe
3.text: Well, ah, last thing I remember is this bizarre THING coming up from right behind me.

4.speaker: Joe
4.text: It was really dark, so I couldn't make out what it was.

5.speaker: Joe
5.text: It attacked, hurt me pretty badly, and then . . . suddenly I'm here with you, feeling just fine.

6.speaker: Mary
6.text: Hmm, that sounds like the thing I just fought off.

7.speaker: Mary
7.text: It seemed like there were two people at first, but when it approached me, it was the only person I could see.

8.speaker: Mary
8.text: Well, I guess if you would call it a person.

10.speaker: Joe
10.text: I'm having a hard time understanding anything that's been going on here.

11.speaker: Joe
11.text: You got rid of it, though?

13.speaker: Mary
13.text: I can't believe it, but . . . I used my knife on it.

14.speaker: Joe
14.text: You mean that pocket knife I got you at the thrift store the other day?

15.speaker: Mary
15.text: Yeah, along with that stupid lantern that YOU wanted to have but then made ME carry.

16.speaker: Joe
16.text: Heh, yeah, sorry again about that.

17.speaker: Joe
17.text: I didn't realize I wouldn't have the space to carry it.

18.speaker: Joe
18.text: I thought it would make our camping trip more authentic.

0.speaker: Mary
0.text: Umm, Joe, your right hand's glowing green.

2.speaker: Mary
2.text: Hey, don't point it at me!

2.speaker: Mary
2.text: Your hand's not glowing anymore, so I think so?

3.speaker: Joe
3.text: Mary, what the heck's going on here?

5.speaker: Mary
5.text: We could speculate, but honestly, I don't really want to waste time.

6.speaker: Joe
6.text: Agree. It sounds like you don't know much more than I do, anyways.

7.speaker: Joe
7.text: All I've been doing is walking around to find anyone or a way out.

8.speaker: Joe
8.text: You've probably already tried, but do you have your phone on you?

9.speaker: Mary
9.text: Yeah, but it won't turn on.

11.speaker: Joe
11.text: Well, regardless, we should get going.

11.speaker: Joe
11.text: I've been rationing food, but it's not like I packed for this.

0.speaker: Joe
0.text: Hey, what happened to us while we were watching the eclipse, that was . . . real, wasn't it?

3.speaker: Mary
3.text: For now, I think we should just accept what's happening and move forward.

5.speaker: Joe
5.text: Maybe someone else will have a better idea, if we even find them before getting out.

6.speaker: Mary
6.text: I . . . don't even want to think about not finding them.
